title: The presumption of innocence
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches bail and remand, and only mentions the presumption of innocence as background, so it does not teach the presumption of innocence or the right to silence that this new point needs.

draft.title: The presumption of innocence
card: A person accused of a crime is treated as innocent until they are proven guilty. They do not have to prove that they did not do it.
The presumption applies to everyone charged, however serious the charge or however strong the claims in the news seem.
The accused also has the right to silence. They can choose not to answer police questions or give evidence at trial.
Staying silent does not prove guilt. The accused is still presumed innocent.
draft.remember: Innocent until proven guilty, and silence is not an admission.

a.q: Tom is charged with burglary in Geelong. Before his trial, how must the law treat him?
opts: As innocent, until he is proven guilty
As guilty, unless he can show he is innocent
As innocent, but only if the charge is minor
As guilty, if he refuses to answer police questions
a.why: The presumption of innocence applies to every accused person until guilt is proven. It is not limited to minor charges, and Tom does not have to prove anything.
a.clue: Who is treated as innocent, and until when?

b.q: Police question Mei about a fire at a Bendigo warehouse. She says she will not answer any questions. What does this silence mean in law?
opts: Nothing: it is her right, and does not prove guilt
It shows she has something to hide and is probably guilty
It is an admission that she started the fire
It removes the presumption of innocence for her
b.why: The right to silence lets an accused person decline to answer without it being treated as guilt. The tempting idea that silence looks suspicious is wrong, because Mei is still presumed innocent.
b.clue: Choosing not to speak is a right, not evidence.

a.best: As innocent, until he is proven guilty

b.best: Nothing: it is her right, and does not prove guilt
